name: @dreamteamer/perspective
description: Read a contributor's own past work — git, agent sessions, tickets, mail, documents — and build the operating model it runs on, for a dreamteamer workspace.

dreamteamer.title: Perspective
dreamteamer.description: Read a contributor's existing work and end with their PERSPECTIVE existing — the operating model their work actually runs on, and a proposal for how to adapt this workspace to track and automate it. One resumable `retrospective-sessions` record walks thirteen stages: `installed`, then `inventoried` (what evidence is reachable — `sources`, `repos`, and the session RECORDS what it saw), `read` (condense every source — `conversations`, `activity-weeks`, `tickets`, `threads`, `deliverables`, and the people behind them as `users`; the workspace is a source too, giving `terms`, `concepts` and `decisions` from its own vocabulary), `clustered` (what was done — `activities` and `topics`), `projected` (`projects`), `extracted` (what was decided and said — `workflows`, more `decisions`, and the vocabulary in two steps: `terms` IDENTIFIED verbatim from the evidence with their spellings and counts, then CLASSIFIED into the `concepts` whose meaning they share — many terms, one concept, and a term left unclassified is an honest residue rather than a gap to paper over), `inferred` (what the work was FOR — `goals`, read backwards out of decisions and activity arcs, never out of what the person said), `found` (what recurs — `findings`, `insights`, and the `assumptions` each one rests on, every assumption carrying the observation that would prove it wrong), `interviewed` (what the evidence cannot settle — `questions`, written before they are asked), `proposed` (what the brain should keep — `proposals`, whose body IS the draft descriptor), `synthesised` (`perspectives`), then `materialised` and `seeded`. ⚠ EVIDENCE AND MODEL RECORDS ARE KEYED BY THE CONTRIBUTOR, not by the run, so a second retrospective UPDATES the operating model rather than writing a parallel copy beside it. ⚠ NOTHING HERE IS AUTHORED TRUTH — every record is what a run FOUND, and `confirmed` is reserved for what a person actually answered. The observed-world collections — `users`, `projects`, `activities`, `goals`, `decisions` and `deliverables` — share the nouns of the authored collections in `users` and `projects`, and every structural reference among them stays inside this namespace. They are PARALLEL objects, never `extends:` overlays: a merged collection could not tell a record a run FOUND from one a person WROTE. Each carries `real` — a ONE-WAY, SOFT reference to the authored record it appears to be, so the correspondence is a proposal a person confirms and the real world never gains a field pointing at a finding. `concepts.classifies` points a MEANING at those observed objects and `concepts.related_to` at the real ones; `terms.mentions` points a WORD at the records it is load-bearing in, which is the narrower question. Every MODEL-tier record also carries the `perspective-observation` quad — `observed` (a date-time, so the whole tier sorts on one axis), `context`, `wrong_if` and a one-way soft `related` — because a model record is a claim about somebody's world at a moment, and the moment, the circumstance, the falsifier and the blast radius are four facts `creation_context` was being asked to carry in one line. The EVIDENCE tier deliberately does not carry it: those rows are counted, never judged. Holds evidence, findings and proposals only, never a domain object; `bin/check-records.mjs` is the guard a consuming workspace chains after `dreamteamer check`.
